pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you do while another speaker is talking in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. Talk loudly
   B. Listen without interrupting
   C. Laugh
   D. Leave

2. What is a hobby? (1 mark)
   A. A punishment
   B. A school rule
   C. A test
   D. Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time

3. Which interjection shows praise? (1 mark)
   A. Ouch
   B. Oops
   C. Yuck
   D. Bravo

4. Which interjection shows a request for silence? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray
   B. Aha
   C. Bravo
   D. Shh

5. Which line is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray Amina: it is Saturday
   B. Amina Hurray! It is Saturday
   C. Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.
   D. It is Saturday Amina Hurray

6. Where can you find correct interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. By copying from another language
   B. By listening to and asking elders and teachers
   C. By inventing them
   D. By guessing

7. What is a call centre? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A farm
   C. A school
   D. A place where staff answer customers' phone calls

8. Which adjective describes size? (1 mark)
   A. soft
   B. red
   C. round
   D. tiny

9. What is good telephone manner? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking clearly and giving your name
   B. Calling very late for no reason
   C. Interrupting
   D. Speaking with food in your mouth

10. What is an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. A word that names a person
   B. A joining word
   C. A word that shows action
   D. A word that describes a noun

11. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. A short eye-catching title
   B. A picture
   C. The last word
   D. A price

12. Which describes an object by size and colour? (1 mark)
   A. Bagging
   B. A bag
   C. To bag
   D. A big red bag

13. What is a form? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A page with spaces for information
   C. A kind of song
   D. A story

14. Where should your class keep collected forms? (1 mark)
   A. In the fire
   B. In a portfolio
   C. Under a stone
   D. In the river

15. Which is a polite way to interrupt? (1 mark)
   A. You are wrong!
   B. Be quiet!
   C. Stop talking!
   D. Excuse me, may I say something?

16. What does a moderator do in a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Guides the discussion and gives turns
   B. Speaks all the time
   C. Sleeps
   D. Leaves

17. What does answer when they call mean in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. A leader sleeps
   B. A leader responds when people need them
   C. A leader hides
   D. A leader shouts

18. What should you use in your answers to poem questions? (1 mark)
   A. Words from the poem
   B. Nothing
   C. A dictionary only
   D. Your favourite song

19. Which is a poor instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Collect the exercise books and place them on the table
   B. Do the thing with the papers
   C. Rinse the soap
   D. Wet your hands

20. What should you do to check if your instructions are clear? (1 mark)
   A. Tear them
   B. Hide them
   C. Ask someone to follow them
   D. Read them backwards

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. List three steps for understanding a poem. (3 marks)

22. Write two polite phrases to interrupt. (2 marks)

23. Write an advert of four sentences for hand-made baskets. Include a headline, two adjectives, a price and where to buy. (5 marks)

24. Describe the steps for creating a form for your class about favourite cultural foods. (5 marks)

25. Compose a four-line poem about a good leader. Make lines two and four rhyme. (4 marks)

26. Explain why you should ask an elder or teacher about writing interjections in your mother tongue, and describe how to collect them. (5 marks)

27. Describe how a panel discussion is organised. (4 marks)

28. Give two rules for filling in a form correctly. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Listen without interrupting
   Good debaters listen.

2. D — Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time
   A hobby is a regular enjoyable activity.

3. D — Bravo
   Bravo praises good work.

4. D — Shh
   Shh asks for quiet.

5. C — Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.
   It has name, colon and words.

6. B — By listening to and asking elders and teachers
   Speakers know the correct forms.

7. D — A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   Call centre staff answer calls.

8. D — tiny
   Tiny describes size.

9. A — Speaking clearly and giving your name
   Clarity and courtesy help.

10. D — A word that describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

11. A — A short eye-catching title
   A headline is the title of an advert or news item.

12. D — A big red bag
   Big and red are adjectives.

13. B — A page with spaces for information
   Forms collect information.

14. B — In a portfolio
   A portfolio keeps them organised.

15. D — Excuse me, may I say something?
   It asks permission politely.

16. A — Guides the discussion and gives turns
   The moderator keeps order.

17. B — A leader responds when people need them
   It means to respond to people's needs.

18. A — Words from the poem
   Answers should come from the poem.

19. B — Do the thing with the papers
   It is vague.

20. C — Ask someone to follow them
   Testing shows whether they work.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read it aloud more than once, find meanings of new words, say the message in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Excuse me, may I say something? Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that?
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any advert with a headline, two adjectives, a price and a place, for example: Strong Baskets for Sale. Our baskets are big and colourful. Only 300 shillings each. Buy at the market gate.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the four required features and one mark for clear sentences.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Decide the purpose, write a title, list questions such as name, class and favourite food, leave space for answers, write short instructions, test it with a friend and improve it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step up to five.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on leadership with two rhyming lines, for example A good leader listens, Speaks the truth each day, Helps the weak and lonely, And shows the proper way.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme and four lines, two marks for rhyme.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask because spelling and meanings must be correct and not invented. Listen to speakers, write each interjection with its feeling on a flashcard, check spelling with the teacher and sort by feeling.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the reason and three marks for collecting steps.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a topic, a moderator and panel members, panel members give opinions in turn, the audience asks questions, the moderator summarises.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Read instructions first, write neatly inside the spaces, give true information, sign and date it (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
